metadata.title: Stocks slide as huge Anthropic IPO unable to calm AI fears

content.text:
Technology stocks led further market declines in Asia and Europe on Friday after the blockbuster Wall Street IPO for Claude maker Anthropic failed to dispel growing worries about the massive investments and sky-high valuations for AI firms.
After its record-breaking initial public offering this week, Anthropic soared 17 percent on its trading debut Thursday.
But futures contracts indicated a drop of more than six percent ahead of Wall Street's reopening, after a broad wave of selling pulled down the overall market Thursday.
"The performance of the shares over the coming days and weeks could provide one of the clearest tests yet of whether investors believe the enormous sums being poured into AI will ultimately generate attractive returns," said Dan Coatsworth, head of markets at AJ Bell.
While Anthropic surged on its Nasdaq debut, the tech-dominated stocks index closed down 1.3 percent overall.
New York's broader S&P 500 shed 2.0 percent as it dropped for a sixth session in a row, its longest losing streak since April 2024, according to Deutsche Bank analyst Jim Reid.
"It's been another hectic and negative week and one where even positive news is struggling to help the market stabilise," Reid said in a research note.
"If we get a seventh fall today, that would make it the longest run of declines since the pandemic slump began in February 2020," he noted.
Traders have also been spooked by the US Commerce Department's move to close a loophole allowing Chinese companies to access Nvidia's powerful AI chips remotely, adding to worries that a new Democratic-led Congress will impose further regulations.
It comes after Nvidia's high-profile founder and CEO Jensen Huang had to resign following revelations of extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy.
In Asian trading Friday, the Tokyo, Seoul and Taipei stock markets -- home to the region's leading AI-linked firms -- tumbled between five and 6.2 percent.
Europe's main stock markets retreated in late morning deals, with shares in French video game maker Ubisoft slumping 12 percent after it posted a bigger first-half loss than expected.
The report came amid the worldwide hype surrounding "Grand Theft Auto VI", the latest in the hugely popular Rockstar Games series that is shaping up to be the biggest entertainment launch ever.
- Key figures at around 1030 GMT -
London - FTSE 100: DOWN 0.5 percent at 10,404.63 points
Paris - CAC 40: DOWN 1.2 percent at 7,986.82
Frankfurt - DAX: DOWN 1.5 percent at 25,075.23
